$comment: The complete vocabulary of the Build surface. Adding a dimension here, with a derive block, is the only way to extend it. No count is fixed: manifest.json lists which dimensions are live in each build (docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md). derive kinds are documented in pipeline/derive.py; fields are the logical names bound in config/pipeline.json. Every dimension states its kind (category, ordered_band or place) and its cardinality; the chart rules read them (config/chart_rules.json).

It counts passenger cars and vans, goods vans, trucks and utes, buses, motor caravans and special purpose vehicles, new and used, and it includes vehicles since removed from the register.

The one exception is a ratio that divides one by the other on purpose, completeness: a measure that says so (ratio_of_clashing_datasets in config/measures.json) is read as one number, not as two series. src/lib/resolve.ts marks any other preset that reads both as invalid.

datasets.$dimension_labels_comment: Registered as is the type NZTA registers a vehicle under, said of a vehicle when it is registered; this dataset counts the register as it stands, where the same field reads as the vehicle's type (D-141).
datasets.$single_period_comment: The dataset has one period, the snapshot's month (docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md, Stock datasets). The chart rules read it as one period (chart_rules.json, facts.periods), so a category counted in it is a ranking and two fields crossed are a grid; a question that would draw it over time is blocked; and a chart of it has no time range, no month to choose, no move, no change on a year ago.

retired_datasets.$comment: Datasets that were joined into another (D-158). Nothing writes one of these ids any more and none is built; an older link, a saved canvas or a Build link still names one, and src/lib/builder.ts (readRetired) reads it as `to`, with `where` kept as conditions of the question: the vehicles the old dataset counted, so the chart draws the same figures. `label` is the name the old dataset had, for the sentence that tells a visitor what became of it. `where` is the old dataset's own scope, as the labels the cube holds (vehicle_scope.csv, in_scope), so a vehicle type brought into scope later changes nothing here. An id is never taken off this list: a link to it must keep working.

dimensions.label: Powertrain
dimensions.public_note: NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full. Mild hybrids are picked out by model name, so the mild hybrid line counts only the ones identified; the note below says what share that is.
dimensions.$note_condition_comment: Both notes speak of a mild hybrid line. A dataset that does not divide its hybrids (manifest: mild_split_published false) has none, so the notes read as the _otherwise ones say; the chart then carries the sentence defaults.phrases.mild_split_withheld. The conditions are listed in src/lib/dimensionNote.ts.
dimensions.public_note_otherwise: NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full.
dimensions.note_otherwise: NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full. This dataset does not divide its hybrids (mild_split_published is false), so they are one value and there is no mild line to relabel.
dimensions.help: How the vehicle is powered: petrol, diesel, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, electric.
dimensions.note: NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full. Mild hybrids are identified by nameplate, so the category takes the label and coverage published in the manifest (mild_hybrid_identification_coverage): 'Mild hybrid (identified)' with its coverage, until coverage is high.

dimensions.label: Powertrain group
dimensions.public_note: Powertrain values put into groups. The group that holds the hybrid and mild hybrid values together is the same whether or not a dataset divides its hybrids. NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full.
dimensions.public_line: Powertrain values are put into groups. A group can hold together values NZTA does not record apart, and it reads the same whether or not a dataset divides them.
dimensions.help: How the vehicle is powered, in groups: a roll-up of powertrain in which each powertrain value sits in one group.
dimensions.$comment: The same motive power as powertrain, read through the same final motive power (after mild_hybrid_models.csv), so a vehicle's group is a function of the powertrain it ends up with: powertrain_map.csv gives each powertrain exactly one group (a test holds it). The value is the label column powertrain_group_label, not powertrain_group: the hybrid classification reads powertrain_group's own values (pipeline.json hybrid_classification.source_hybrid), and one of them is also a powertrain value. The mild split does not touch it (derive.undivide_hybrids moves only the column that looks up the powertrain column), so it is published where the split is withheld. An unmapped or not-recorded motive power reads as it does for powertrain.

dimensions.label: Brand
dimensions.help: The badge on the car. Normalised via the brand registry.

dimensions.label: Manufacturer group
dimensions.$cardinality_comment: high, like make: 43 named groups in the 2026-08 cube, every one with vehicles in the last 12 months, the 14 largest holding 88% of those vehicles. A single 12-month window of competitors is drawn as a ranking (league), as for brands; longer periods stay a mix chart (D-050).
dimensions.help: Who owns the brand. Toyota, Lexus and Daihatsu all roll up to Toyota Group.

dimensions.label: Brand owned from
dimensions.help: The home country of the company that owns the brand today, or for a defunct brand the last company that built it. Volvo counts as China here.

dimensions.label: Brand originally from
dimensions.help: Where the brand was founded. Volvo counts as Sweden here.

dimensions.label: Built in
dimensions.public_note: Where a vehicle was built is not recorded for almost every vehicle first registered before late 1985, and is recorded for almost all since. The grey line near the top of the chart until then is that gap in the record, not where vehicles came from.
dimensions.public_line: Where a vehicle was built is not recorded for almost every older vehicle, so the grey line near the top of the chart is a gap in the record, not where vehicles came from.
dimensions.help: The country where the vehicle was principally manufactured. A Toyota built in Thailand counts as Thailand.

dimensions.label: Imported from
dimensions.help: Where a used import was registered before coming to NZ.

dimensions.label: Vehicle type
dimensions.help: Car, ute, van, truck or other. Most SUVs are recorded as station wagons, so they count as cars. Other includes buses, motor caravans, special purpose vehicles and passenger three-wheelers.
dimensions.$comment: segment_map matches on vehicle_type + body_type. Where gvm_min_kg/gvm_max_kg are set, GVM must fall in that inclusive range and a missing GVM matches nothing; where both are blank, GVM is not used.

dimensions.label: Vehicle class
dimensions.help: Light passenger, light commercial, heavy commercial or other, from type, body and mass; utes and vans fall in all three. Other includes buses, motor caravans and special purpose vehicles of any mass.
dimensions.$comment: The same segment_map.csv match as segment, reading its segment_group column, so powertrain-mix can narrow to light passenger vehicles. segment = Car is not light passenger: light passenger also holds the passenger-registered utes and vans.

dimensions.label: Registered as
dimensions.public_line: The type NZTA registers each vehicle under, which is a different thing from a split that also reads the body and the weight.
dimensions.public_note: The type NZTA registers the vehicle under. It is a different thing from Vehicle type, which sorts vehicles into cars, utes, vans and trucks from the body and weight as well: a ute can be registered as a passenger vehicle. Only the types a dataset counts are shown: the five types of the wider scope in the vehicles still registered and in true registrations on the wider scope, the two types of the default scope in true registrations, and every type in the vehicles registered today.
dimensions.help: The type NZTA registers the vehicle under, such as passenger cars and vans. It is not the car, ute, van and truck split of Vehicle type, which also reads the body type and weight.
dimensions.$comment: The lookup reads the same vehicle_scope.csv key that decides which vehicles are in scope, so it cannot meet a type that scope does not know (the build aborts on one). Only the types a dataset's scope counts reach its slice (every type reaches the slice of the stock, fleet, which has no scope); a type brought into scope later appears under its label with no other change. A series source carries no register field, so the dimension is not live for registrations_cars_long_run (derive.applicable), with no applies_to.

dimensions.label: Passenger or commercial
dimensions.public_note: Passenger vehicles are the vehicles NZTA registers as passenger cars and vans. Commercial is every other type this dataset counts: goods vans, trucks and utes, buses, motor caravans and special purpose vehicles. It follows the type a vehicle is registered under, so a ute registered as a passenger vehicle is a passenger vehicle here.
dimensions.public_line: Each vehicle is placed in a group by the type NZTA registers it under, so a vehicle that looks like one kind but is registered as another takes the group of its registered type.
dimensions.help: Whether the vehicle is registered as a passenger car or van, or as one of the other types this dataset counts. Commercial here is every counted type but passenger.
dimensions.$comment: The same vehicle_scope.csv key as vehicle_type, reading the trade_group column the file gives each type of the trade scope. A type outside that scope has no group and never reaches this dataset. The dataset is the only one that names it (D-113, D-158).

dimensions.label: New or used
dimensions.help: Whether the vehicle was new or second-hand when it first entered NZ.

dimensions.label: New or ex-overseas
dimensions.public_note: New cars are Stats NZ's total less the cars previously registered overseas.
dimensions.source: statsnz:cars total + statsnz:cars previously registered overseas + reference:import_status_map
dimensions.help: Whether the car was new when it entered NZ or had been registered overseas first, as Stats NZ counts them. The two values carry the same names as new or used on the other datasets, so they can be set side by side.

dimensions.label: Engine size (Stats NZ bands)
dimensions.public_note: The bands cover new and ex-overseas cars together.
dimensions.source: statsnz:cars by engine size (seven bands) + reference:statsnz_series
dimensions.help: Engine size in the seven bands Stats NZ uses, from up to 850 cc to 5001 cc and over. These are not the engine size bands of the other datasets.

dimensions.label: Region
dimensions.help: The region where the registered owner lives now, from their most recent address. Not where the vehicle is used, and not necessarily where the owner lived when it was first registered.

dimensions.label: Current use
dimensions.public_line: What NZTA records each vehicle as being used for at the snapshot date, which can change over a vehicle's life.
dimensions.public_note: What NZTA records each vehicle as being used for, in NZTA's own broad groups, each shown by its words. It is the latest use recorded at the snapshot date, not the use when the vehicle was first registered, and it can change over a vehicle's life: for rental the two are shown to differ, and for the other groups they have not been compared. It describes the vehicle, not the owner's address or anything else about the owner. Small counts are hidden, and so are other counts that would give a hidden one away.
dimensions.help: How NZTA records the vehicle as used now: private passenger, rental, taxi or commercial passenger, goods groups, agricultural, emergency and other. Counted over the vehicles registered today and never by when a vehicle was first registered.
dimensions.$comment: An owner field (config/data_map.json, VEHICLE_USAGE): its slice is written under the small-cell rule, and its pair with vehicle type under the rule for a table of two fields (D-127, D-135). It describes the vehicle as at the snapshot, so the data map marks the field stock_only and only a stock dataset (fleet) is offered it; applies_to names that dataset and the build aborts if it names another. The labels are NZTA's own words (vehicle_usage_map.csv). A new raw value has no row in the file, reads __UNMAPPED__ and trips the unmapped guard (pipeline.json guardrails.abort_on_unmapped).

dimensions.label: Vehicle age
dimensions.public_note: Age on the snapshot date, not when the vehicle was bought. It is counted from the year NZTA records for each vehicle, not from when it was built: for a vehicle sold new here since 2007, the year it was first registered here; for a used import, a year from its life overseas, usually when it was built or first registered there. For vehicles sold new here before 2007 that year is less consistent, sometimes a year early. A year, not a date, so an age can be out by a year.
dimensions.public_line: Age on the snapshot date, counted from the year NZTA records for each vehicle and not from a date, so an age can be out by a year.
dimensions.help: Years since the vehicle year. For NZ-new vehicles first registered from 2007 that is years since first registration; for used imports, years since the vehicle's year overseas. Vehicle year is less consistent for NZ-new vehicles registered before 2007.
dimensions.$comment: min and max are inclusive; max null means no upper bound. A missing VEHICLE_YEAR, a VEHICLE_YEAR of 0, or a negative result (vehicle years after the snapshot exist) falls to unknown.

dimensions.label: Engine size
dimensions.help: Engine capacity in bands. Electric vehicles fall in a separate 'none' band.
dimensions.basis: CC_RATING, for powertrains with has_combustion_engine = true in powertrain_map
dimensions.$comment: min and max are inclusive cc; max null means no upper bound. A powertrain without a combustion engine is 'none' whatever CC_RATING says (14% of BEVs record a small non-zero CC). An engined vehicle whose CC is missing or below the lowest min (0, and implausible values such as 1 or 19 cc that appear in the data) is unknown.

dimensions.label: Age when first registered here
dimensions.public_note: Age when first registered in New Zealand, counted from the year NZTA records for each vehicle. A vehicle sold new here since 2007 is 0 years old by definition, because that year is its first registration here; for a used import it is a year from its life overseas, usually when it was built or first registered there. For vehicles sold new here before 2007 that year is less consistent, sometimes a year early. A year, not a date, so an age can be out by a year. Counted among vehicles still registered at the snapshot: arrivals from earlier years have had longer to leave the register, and vehicles do not all leave at the same rate, so the longer the span, the more the ages shown may differ from those that arrived at the time.
dimensions.public_line: Age when first registered in New Zealand, counted from the year NZTA records, so an age can be out by a year; a vehicle sold new here in recent years is zero by definition. Ages are counted among vehicles still registered, so the longer ago they arrived, the more they may differ from those that arrived.
dimensions.help: How old the vehicle was when it was first registered in New Zealand. Zero means new.
dimensions.$comment: min and max are inclusive years; max null means no upper bound. Single years to 19 because the moving cutoff and odd-age bumps are one year wide (MODEL_AND_AGE.md section 3). A missing VEHICLE_YEAR, a VEHICLE_YEAR of 0 and a negative result each fall to unknown and are counted separately in the manifest (MODEL_AND_AGE.md section 5).

dimensions.label: Imported or assembled here
dimensions.public_note: NZTA's flag for whether a vehicle was assembled or built in New Zealand or imported built up. It is a flag, not a place: a vehicle assembled here from an imported kit records the kit's country as where it was built. Recording starts in late 1995, so vehicles first registered before then show as not recorded, and the grey line near the top of the chart until then is that gap in the record. Very few vehicles first registered in recent years are marked as assembled here, so their figures rest on small counts.
dimensions.public_line: NZTA's flag for whether a vehicle was assembled in New Zealand or arrived already built. It is a flag, not a place, and it is not recorded for older vehicles, which show as not recorded.
dimensions.help: Whether NZTA records the vehicle as imported built up or as assembled or built in New Zealand. Not where it was built: see Built in.
dimensions.$comment: UNKNOWN is a sentinel (sentinels.csv), so it reads as not recorded; a new raw value has no row in nz_assembled_map.csv and trips the unmapped guard (pipeline.json guardrails.abort_on_unmapped). A series source carries no register field, so the dimension is not live for registrations_cars_long_run, and the dashboard export has none, so it is not live for the two flow datasets (derive.applicable), with no applies_to.

dimensions.label: NZTA vehicle class
dimensions.public_note: NZTA's vehicle equipment standard class, shown as NZTA's label with its code in brackets. The labels are from NZTA's vehicle classes page, as supplied by the maintainer on 17 November 2026; OTH is not in the supplied table and is shown as its code. The class is the one NZTA recorded: it is not checked against the vehicle's mass or seats. Recording is patchy before 2002 and differs between new and used vehicles, so the mix of classes before then, and the vehicles with no class recorded, show what was recorded, not what was registered. NA is a class code, not a missing value. A class almost always sits under one type of vehicle, so setting the two side by side shows the same split twice.
dimensions.public_line: NZTA's vehicle equipment standard class, as NZTA recorded it and not checked against the vehicle; recording is patchy for older vehicles, so older figures show what was recorded.
dimensions.help: NZTA's vehicle equipment standard class: NZTA's label with the code in brackets. The labels and definitions are from NZTA's vehicle classes page, supplied by the maintainer on 17 November 2026. OTH is not in the supplied table and is shown as its code.
dimensions.$comment: A blank class is the only form of not recorded: it reads __UNDEFINED__ and sentinels.csv lists none for this field, because NA is a real class (NZTA's light goods vehicle) and must never be treated as one. class_map.csv holds every code on the whole register and the classes NZTA defines that the register did not carry in October 2026, so a vehicle type brought into scope later, or a defined class that first appears, does not trip the unmapped guard, and a code the table does not hold does (pipeline.json guardrails.abort_on_unmapped). Not live for the datasets whose source carries no class (derive.applicable), with no applies_to.

dimensions.label: Seats
dimensions.public_note: The number of seats NZTA records, in bands. Seats are not recorded for many of the vehicles first registered from early 1994 to late 1995, so the not-recorded part is large for those months and small otherwise. A count of zero is not recorded, and a count above 60 is not taken as a number of seats: both are counted as not recorded.
dimensions.public_line: The number of seats NZTA records, in bands. Seats are not recorded for many vehicles first registered in one short span of months, and a count of zero, or one too large to be a number of seats, is counted as not recorded.
dimensions.help: How many seats NZTA records for the vehicle, in bands from 1-2 to 8 or more.
dimensions.basis: NUMBER_OF_SEATS, inside the guard of 1 to 60
dimensions.$comment: min and max are inclusive; the top band stops at the guard (60), so a count above it, which is not a number of seats, falls to unknown. A zero is the form of not recorded (sentinels.csv), so it is NULL by the time it is banded and falls to unknown too; the manifest counts the two causes apart (bands.seats_band.source_sentinel, out_of_bands). No mean or median is built.

dimensions.label: Power
dimensions.public_note: Engine or motor power in kilowatts, in bands. NZTA records power for vehicles sold new in New Zealand: almost no used import has one, so they show as not recorded. Among new passenger cars and vans, and new goods vehicles of 3.5 tonnes or less, almost none has a power before 1994, most do in 1994 and 1995, and from 1996 nearly all do. About half of heavier new goods vehicles have none. A power of zero is not recorded, and a value outside 5 to 900 kW is not taken as a power: both are counted as not recorded.
dimensions.public_line: Engine or motor power in kilowatts, in bands. NZTA records it for most vehicles sold new in New Zealand, though not for the oldest ones or for many heavier goods vehicles, and almost never for the rest, which show as not recorded.
dimensions.help: The power NZTA records for the vehicle, in kilowatts and in bands from under 75 kW to 500 kW and over. Recorded for vehicles sold new here only.
dimensions.basis: POWER_RATING, inside the guard of 5 to 900 kW
dimensions.$comment: min and max are inclusive kW; the top band stops at the guard (900), so a value above it, which includes the placeholder 999, falls to unknown, as does one below 5. A zero is the form of not recorded (sentinels.csv), so it is NULL by the time it is banded and falls to unknown too; the manifest counts the causes apart (bands.power_band.source_sentinel, out_of_bands). The field is recorded for NZ-new vehicles only (docs/DATA_MAP.md): the pipeline does not look at the import status, so the few used imports that have a value keep it. No mean or median is built.

dimensions.label: Gearbox
dimensions.public_note: The kind of gearbox NZTA records, in four groups: automatic, manual, continuously variable and other. NZTA records it for vehicles sold new in New Zealand: almost no used import has one, so they show as not recorded. Among new passenger cars and vans, and new goods vehicles of 3.5 tonnes or less, almost none has one before 1995, few do in 1995, and from 1996 nearly all do. About half of heavier new goods vehicles have none. Other is NZTA's own value OTHER, which the register does not explain, so it is shown as Other and not put with the automatic, manual or continuously variable gearboxes; most of the vehicles it holds are battery electric.
dimensions.public_line: The kind of gearbox NZTA records, in groups. NZTA records it for most vehicles sold new in New Zealand, though not for the oldest ones or for many heavier goods vehicles, and almost never for the rest, which show as not recorded.
dimensions.help: The kind of gearbox NZTA records for the vehicle, in four groups. Recorded for vehicles sold new here only.
dimensions.$comment: A group, not the number of gears: transmission_map.csv gives each of NZTA's 28 values one group and a label of its own, and the dimension publishes the group. A blank is the only form of not recorded and sentinels.csv lists none for the field. A new raw value has no row in the file and trips the unmapped guard (pipeline.json guardrails.abort_on_unmapped). The field is recorded for NZ-new vehicles only (docs/DATA_MAP.md): the pipeline does not look at the import status, so the few used imports that have a value keep it. Not live for the datasets whose source carries no gearbox (derive.applicable), with no applies_to.

dimensions.label: Colour as recorded
dimensions.public_note: The vehicle's main colour, in NZTA's colour words. The register does not say when the colour was recorded, so it may be the colour the vehicle had when first registered or a later one. A vehicle with no colour recorded shows as not recorded.
dimensions.public_line: The vehicle's main colour in NZTA's colour words. The register does not say when the colour was recorded, so it may not be the colour at first registration.
dimensions.help: The vehicle's main colour as NZTA records it, in NZTA's words. Whether it is the colour at first registration or today's is not shown by the register.
dimensions.$comment: A raw dimension: the values are NZTA's own colour words, published as the register holds them, with no reference file. NULL reads __UNDEFINED__ (sentinels.csv lists no form for the field). A colour NZTA adds later is a new value, not an unmapped one, so the dimension is not in abort_on_unmapped. Not live for the datasets whose source carries no colour (derive.applicable), with no applies_to: the dashboard export and the Stats NZ table have none, and the fleet lists the dimensions it is offered.

dimensions.label: Model
dimensions.help: The nameplate, as brand and model. Only the models with the most vehicles over the trailing 12 months, counted as the dataset counts them, keep their name; the rest are grouped as other. The cap is in this dimension's derive block and every build publishes it. Never use submodel, which is free text.
dimensions.note_template: Only the {dataset.model_cap.model.cap} models with the most {words.cap_count} in the trailing {dataset.coverage_trailing.window_months} months are named, so older months are mostly grouped as other and historical coverage is partial. Named models cover {dataset.model_cap.model.coverage_trailing|pct} of trailing volume and {dataset.model_cap.model.coverage_all_time|pct} of all-time volume.

periods.label: All time
periods.$comment: No months: runs from the dataset's first month to the latest snapshot.

rules.$comment: Shape is inferred from measure + dimension. See CLAUDE.md Shapes. There is no limit on the number of conditions a question carries (D-062, D-107): a key that said two was read by nothing and was removed.
